parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, evacuation, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a fuller incident report within 10 business days. Other confirmed thermal incidents shall be reported within 10 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and promptly provide updated information as the investigation proceeds.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, evacuation, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a fuller incident report within 10 business days. S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, evacuation, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a fuller incident report within 10 business days. Other confirmed thermal incidents shall be reported within 10 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers within 5 business days when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and promptly provide updated information as the investigation proceeds. Reports shall include available unit and model identification, incident circumstances, and known injuries or damage.

parameters.quote: A model passes only if no more than 5% of tested units fail. Manufacturers shall provide full per-model results, test method, sample size, and test date to the regulator and directly to customers considering purchase of that model; individual-company per-model failure rates shall not be published to the general public. Regulators may publish aggregated or anonymized results. A model exceeding 5% shall undergo corrective action and a passing retest before further market placement.

parameters.quote: All new units shall support remote emergency shut-off no later than 12 months after adoption. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units to provide remote emergency shut-off, where technically feasible, within 6 years after adoption. Where retrofit is not feasible, the manufacturer shall notify affected customers and the regulator and provide an equivalent documented emergency response measure.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: All new units shall support remote emergency shut-off no later than 12 months after adoption. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units to provide remote emergency shut-off, where technically feasible, within 6 years after adoption. Where retrofit is not feasible, the manufacturer shall notify affected customers and the regulator and provide an equivalent documented emergency response measure.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: All new units shall support remote emergency shut-off no later than 12 months after adoption. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units to provide remote emergency shut-off, where technically feasible, within 6 years after adoption. Where retrofit is not feasible, the manufacturer shall notify affected customers and the regulator and provide an equivalent documented emergency response measure. Shut-off capability must not prevent emergency responders or users from safely isolating a unit locally.

parameters.quote: All new units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall provide installation and maintenance instructions and disclose any relevant limitations to customers.

parameters.quote: If a model’s rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify regulators and affected customers and submit a corrective-action plan for regulator review. A mandatory recall is triggered if the rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, or if the regulator determines that a serious imminent risk requires recall. Recall remedies shall include repair, replacement, or refund.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: If a model’s rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify regulators and affected customers and submit a corrective-action plan for regulator review. A mandatory recall is triggered if the rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, or if the regulator determines that a serious imminent risk requires recall. Recall remedies shall include repair, replacement, or refund.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase, customers shall receive clear instructions for safe installation, operation, and emergency response, plus any model-specific safety precautions. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks, incidents, corrective actions, and recall instructions, using direct contact where practicable. For each model, the annual thermal-incident rate shall be calculated as confirmed thermal incidents during the preceding 12 months per 100,000 units of that model installed and in service during that period; manufacturers shall report the underlying incident and installed-unit counts to regulators. If a model’s rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify regulators and affected customers and submit a corrective-action plan for regulator review. A mandatory recall is triggered if the rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, or if the regulator determines that a serious imminent risk requires recall. Recall remedies shall include repair, replacement, or refund.

judge_section_notes: The final deal adopts a 5% 55°C test-failure limit with per-model results to regulators and prospective customers but no general-public publication, satisfying both companies' disclosure red lines. Remote shut-off is required on new units within 12 months and retrofit within 6 years, while fire suppression is required from 36 months. Recall is mandatory above 8 incidents/100k with prompt notice, hitting Halcyon's Ember 8 but leaving Northwind's Hearth 10 below the trigger; Northwind's Hearth 10 fails the 5% test but can return after corrective action and retest.
